extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and applicants seeking NIH grant funding (R01, R21, K99, DP2/DP5, SBIR/STTR, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, community-sourced guidance on interpreting eRA Commons statuses, interacting with Program Officers and Grants Management Specialists, preparing JIT and resubmissions, and other NIH award-process decisions and timelines. Covers multiple NIH mechanisms (R01/R21/K99/DP/SBIR) and end-of-fiscal-year considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting eRA Commons statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Different Commons statuses have different meanings: 'Pending' or 'Pending administrative review' vs 'Pending Council review' vs 'Council review complete' vs 'Award prepared'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it just says 'Pending' or 'Pending administrative review', your application is being processed for an award and you should receive a JIT request if needed. 'Pending Council review' means someone needs to look at what is going on — contact your PO. 'Council review complete' often indicates no award was made (no email may be sent). 'Award prepared' means final processing steps are underway and a Notice of Award (NoA) is next; final sign-off still required.

rubrics_metrics.name: What 'Pending administrative review' indicates
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pending administrative review' means they are processing the application for possible funding; not a guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review can reveal issues (duplicate funding, regulatory approvals, ineligibility) that could block an award. This status can last weeks to months; the Grants Management Specialist (GMS) handles processing (PO may be out of loop). For supplements, processing is typically faster than full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact your Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the PO for status clarification, resubmission strategy, or if you need advice on SRG selection; but time communications appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait for the summary statement before detailed strategy discussions. It's reasonable to check in periodically (e.g., late July for summer decisions) but POs may be deliberately vague. POs can advise whether to prepare an A1 and can give strategic input based on familiarity with the study section and summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Management Specialist (GMS) is the correct contact for processing questions
rubrics_metrics.description: GMS, not PO, manages application processing, award preparation, and NoA revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GMS asks for fine-grain financial details, that is good progress. Do not over-contact GMS/PO about routine delays — inquiries rarely speed processing. GMS will let you know if additional information is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT (Just-in-Time) timing and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit JIT only when requested and submit required materials as soon as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If JIT is requested, respond immediately; awards can be processed with very short lead time near fiscal year end. Start obtaining regulatory approvals (IACUC, IRB) in advance because if JIT materials are not ready when requested, your application may be skipped. Do not proactively submit JIT before request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date on application/NoA is not an expiration date
rubrics_metrics.description: The start date you list on the application is not binding and is not an expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards can be issued up to September 30 and sometimes with less than the automated 60 days lead time; for FY transitions, timing is flexible and FOA-specific instructions should be read carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategy (A0 vs A1) after an unfundable or ND outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice between submitting a new (A0) vs amended/resubmission (A1) depends on score, reviewer comments, and PO guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High initial scores followed by ND on resubmission are possible. With a high first-score (e.g., 45) you might try either A0 or A1; consult your PO for guidance. If Significance is consistently rated low, consider reframing the question or changing study section (SRG). If PO suggests preparing an A1, ask for strategic advice based on summary statement/panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting and requesting an SRG (study section)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can and should pick your SRG via the PHS Assignment Request Form; CSR/SRO review requests and may accept or decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers never see the assignment request — only CSR and the SRO. Use the CSR Assisted Referral Tool (paste your abstract) to get a ranked list. CSR generally honors requests but may refuse for reasons such as SRG reorganizations, appropriateness of assignment, panel membership transitions, or balancing workloads. You can inquire why a request was not honored but CSR's decision is final; option to withdraw application exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting payline information and funding likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines vary by IC and investigator category (e.g., ESI vs all investigators); published paylines are guidance but can change with appropriations and IC decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A published payline (e.g., NINDS 16% for all investigators, 25% for ESI R01s) is not a hard guarantee. ICs may set different operational paylines depending on budget. Even apps near payline may not be funded due to programmatic priorities. Ask the PO for context but they may not be able to predict final funding certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special FOA restrictions (e.g., no A1 allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some FOAs only accept new applications and do not allow resubmissions (A1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait for the summary statement before contacting PO; if FOA prohibits resubmission, do not submit an A1 to that FOA even if you could meet a shortened window. Instead, rework the proposal for a different FOA in consultation with the PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for summary statement release timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements typically take up to 6–8 weeks after the study section meeting to be issued, but there is no official fixed timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COVID-19 has lengthened typical turnaround times. If you haven't received it after a longer-than-expected period, you can check with the SRO, but it may not speed issuance. Use the waiting period productively (update science, manuscripts, training plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing concise responses when PO requests rebuttal or materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO requests responses to reviewer weaknesses (e.g., 'no firm page limit but pls be concise'), provide focused, succinct materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 1–3 page concise response (one-page intro for A1 plus a slightly longer comprehensive response) is advised; be quick and clear to allow rapid consideration and potential select-pay processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoA revisions and likelihood of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: NoA salaries or budgets can be amended if there was a mistake (vs intentional change); the GMS can reissue a revised NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How long a NoA revision takes depends on GMS workload and required sign-offs. Your grants administrator should coordinate with GMS and GMO chain if necessary. Quick revisions have occurred but delays are common—especially at fiscal year-end or during COVID.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR Fast-Track Phase I/II financial handling
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR Fast Track treats Phase I and Phase II as separate grants; money is tied to the grant period in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You generally cannot carry Phase I funds into Phase II. Request a no-cost extension if you need more time for Phase I (which may delay Phase II start). For Phase II, unspent first-year funds usually carry into the second year automatically; if first-year spending is <75% of budget, justify under-spending in the RPPR or risk budget adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using IC transfers as a positive signal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is transferred to another institute/IC, this can be a sign that the receiving IC is considering funding it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers often occur when another IC's portfolio is a better fit or when an IC is interested in championing an application; contact the PO at the new IC for advice. Awards can be made up to Sept 30 and sometimes late in the year; be prepared for rapid JIT turnaround if transferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-fiscal-year timing and award processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and select-pay decisions often occur late in the fiscal year (Aug–Sept) and timing depends heavily on IC budget availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director's awards and IC late picks happen in August/September; processing can be rapid, so have JIT and regulatory approvals ready. COVID-19 has slowed all processes, and ICs may operate at CR levels until appropriations are finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to act if you don't receive an award notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Not receiving an email or explicit notification does not always mean you were funded; eRA Commons status and PO/GMS communications are informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect you weren't funded, begin preparing a resubmission/ new application so you don't miss the next submission deadline. POs do not always inform applicants that they were not funded; some applicants receive no direct notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: When administrative details indicate forward progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests from GMS for detailed financial information or changes to budget are good signs that award processing is underway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After adjustments, GMS puts award in line for Director review and final approval. There may still be a delay between 'Award prepared' and NoA issuance while sign-offs occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical advice about contacting folks during delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive inquiries to PO/GMS rarely speed things up; targeted, timely questions are better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to plan (e.g., resubmission timing), politely check in with your PO at reasonable intervals. If the PO has indicated 'radio silence until decisions', wait unless you need actionable guidance for resubmission timing.
